chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Do not spend the nights of Tashriq anywhere except in Mina. If you spend the night elsewhere, then a dam (blood sacrifice) is upon you. If you leave at the beginning of the night, you must not be absent from Mina when the night is half gone, unless a ritual duty (nusk) occupies you or you have already left Mecca. And if you leave after the middle of the night, it does not harm you if you spend the morning elsewhere.

key_terms.أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ: The beginning of the night (after sunset)
key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah) following Eid al-Adha
key_terms.دَمٌ: Dam, a sacrificial animal (usually a sheep or goat) offered as a penalty for missing a ritual obligation
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the nights of Tashriq
key_terms.نُسُكٌ: Ritual duty or act of worship (such as stoning the Jamarat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and penalty for not staying in Mina during the nights of Tashriq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Isbibar establishes the mandatory nature of staying in Mina during the nights of Tashriq, linking the penalty of 'dam' (sacrificial animal) to the specific act of departing before the middle of the night. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the precise timing of ritual obligations, distinguishing between early departure which incurs a penalty and late departure after midnight which allows for flexibility, thereby underscoring the integration of temporal precision with spiritual devotion in Hajj rituals.
